subject: Packaging options and pilot request
messages:
From: Amir Qureshi <amir@aurelia.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options and pilot request

Hi Nikhil —

We're evaluating Redwood to replace parts of our inference stack and I wanted to get your advice on packaging. We run two classes of production traffic:

- Interactive user-facing flows (peaky, low-latency)
- Batch / analytics queries (high token volumes, tolerant to higher latency)

A few specific questions:
1) Should we go with a reserved ScaleTier (dedicated capacity) or lean on Throughput Lanes (metered) and use caching?
2) Are advanced features (prefix/KV cache, per-route routing, audit logs) bundled or add-ons? How do they affect list price?
3) What does a minimal pilot look like (length, cost, SLA)?

We'd like to keep predictability on spend while allowing overflow to metered lanes. Also curious about multi-month commit discounts — our procurement prefers a single predictable monthly invoice.

I attached a small usage snapshot from the last 60 days (summary). Can you share a short commercial sketch and pilot plan? We aim to select a vendor by end of April.

Thanks,
Amir
VP Product | Aurelia Labs
A: 415-555-0182

Attachment: aurelia-usage-summary.csv (csv)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Qureshi <amir@aurelia.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options and pilot request

Hi Amir —

Thanks for the detail — this is a classic mix and we can support both predictability and overflow. High level options (short):

1) Reserved ScaleTier (recommended if predictability + consistent low latency matter)
   - Dedicated GPU pool sized to your 95th percentile throughput
   - Anchor discount for monthly commit (6/12 months)
   - Bundled features: KV/prefix cache and basic routing. Audit logs are available as an add-on.

2) Throughput Lanes (best for elastic/batch):
   - Metered per-token with volume breakpoints; no upfront capacity commitment
   - Good overflow path for spikes and non-latency-sensitive workloads

3) Hybrid: commit to a smaller reserved tier for interactive flows + Throughput Lanes for batch. This gives predictable spend for core SLAs and keeps marginal cost low for analytic jobs.

Commercial sketches I attached (Aurelia_Packaging_Options_v1.pdf) and a pilot SLA table (pilot-sla-table.xlsx). Quick asks so I can refine pricing:
- Target monthly committed spend or target headroom (e.g., want 2x peak to avoid throttles?)
- Data residency / retention needs (audit logs + retention windows)
- Is a 6-week pilot sufficient to validate routing + cache behavior?

Next step: I can draft two commercial options (12-mo commit with deeper discount vs 6-mo with stepdown credits) and loop legal on data residency. Ben, Kimberly — any commercial guardrails or standard concessions we should consider?

Best,
Nikhil
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurelia_Packaging_Options_v1.pdf (pdf), pilot-sla-table.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Amir Qureshi <amir@aurelia.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options and pilot request

Nikhil / team —

This is a good starting point. A couple of commercial notes from my side:

- For customers who want predictability, our typical play is a 6- or 12-month committed throughput with stepdown credits and an option to carry over a limited portion.
- We can offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset the pilot cost (usually 10-20% of the first month) if they sign a 12-month commit.
- Approval for a 20% list discount requires a 12-month revenue run-rate target (I can share the thresholds).

Nikhil — please produce two succinct sketches: (A) 12-month commit @ target RR + feature bundle (what's included/excluded), (B) 6-month commit with higher unit price but flexible stepdown. Include a minimal SLA additive cost for audit logs/data retention. Attach a ballpark quote so procurement can start budgeting.

Kimberly — can you confirm if we should include a managed onboarding add-on (hours) and whether Audit+Retention should be billed as a recurring item or per-GB overage?

Ben
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment: quote-AU-2027-088.pdf (pdf)

From: Amir Qureshi <amir@aurelia.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Lina Morales <lina@aurelia.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options and pilot request

Thanks, team. Quick clarifications:

- Our preference is predictable monthly invoicing but we want a mechanism to offload batch to metered lanes without breaking the budget. The hybrid seems attractive.
- Procurement will push for the 12-month term if we can get ~20% off list and some onboarding credit. They also need a simple stepdown formula tied to usage thresholds (e.g., 90/75/50% of committed throughput).
- We have strict 7-year audit retention requirements for a subset of telemetry — that will likely be billed as an add-on. Can you outline the per-GB vs recurring options?

Yes, a 6-week pilot works. Timeline: procurement review in late April; aim to have commercial sketch + PO-ready quote by April 12 so I can raise early.

Appreciate it —
Amir

On a separate note: Lina, can you share the internal procurement checklist so we align on the docs they’ll request?

---
Aurelia Labs
Attachment: none

Overflow to Throughput Lanes priced at a reduced metered rate.

2) 6-month committed throughput (Hybrid) — 12% off list, larger onboarding credit applied to pilot, stepdown credits at 90/75/50% tiers. Audit retention priced both as per-GB overage and a recurring retention package (I’ll show both).
